::: {.page-intro}
The Shu Lab is based in Pittsburgh and works across UPMC and Brown collaborations. We study stroke prevention, neuroendovascular outcomes, cerebrovascular epidemiology, clinical AI, and recovery through a translational, team-science approach.
:::

## About Liqi Shu

Liqi Shu, MD, is a [vascular neurologist at the UPMC Stroke Institute](https://providers.upmc.com/provider/liqi-shu/4838362), core faculty in [Pitt Cerebrovascular Medicine](https://www.neurology.pitt.edu/clinical-divisions/cerebrovascular-medicine), and an [Adjunct Instructor in Neurology at Brown University](https://vivo.brown.edu/display/lshu). He completed neurology residency and vascular neurology fellowship at Rhode Island Hospital/Brown, followed by the 2024–25 NIH StrokeNet SPIRIT research fellowship and neurointerventional training at UPMC.

His background in computer science and biology shapes a program that treats clinical data, imaging, language, EEG, and human movement as complementary signals. The lab's completed work spans validated peri-procedural stroke prediction, large-language-model chart abstraction, international cerebrovascular registries, and machine-learning measures of post-stroke arm use.

Dr. Shu received a 2023 [Brown Dean's Excellence Award](https://biomedical.brown.edu/about-division/leadership/office-dean/excellence-awards) for teaching and mentoring in the Neurology Clerkship.

## Our principles

::: {.focus-grid .principles-grid}
::: {.focus-card}
### Start with the clinical need
The strongest analytic question begins with a decision patients and clinicians actually face.
:::
::: {.focus-card}
### Match the method to the question
We combine real-world evidence, registries, imaging, and quantitative models without treating any one method as the answer to everything.
:::
::: {.focus-card}
### Build collaboratively
Clinical insight, statistical rigor, engineering, and trainee curiosity are all part of the work.
:::
::: {.focus-card}
### Aim for translation
We favor outputs that can become better risk estimates, workflows, tools, and ultimately better care.
:::
:::
